description_full: TriMas Corporation engages in the design, development, manufacture, and sale of products for consumer products, aerospace and defense, and industrial markets worldwide. The company operates through Packaging and Specialty Products segments. The Packaging segment offers dispensing products, such as foaming and sanitizer pumps, lotion and hand soap pumps, beverage dispensers, perfume sprayers, and nasal and trigger sprayers; polymeric and steel caps and closures comprising food lids, flip-top and beverage closures, child resistance caps, drum and pail closures, and flexible spouts; polymeric jar products; integrated dispensers; bag-in-box products; and consumable vascular delivery and diagnostic test components under the Rieke, Taplast, Affaba & Ferrari, Aarts Packaging, Intertech, Omega Plastics, and Rapak brands. The Specialty Products segment designs, manufactures, and distributes steel cylinders for use in transportation, storage, and dispensing of packaged and compressed gases under the Norris Cylinder brand. It sells its products through a direct sales force, third-party agents, and distributors. The company was incorporated in 1986 and is headquartered in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan.

financial_summary: TriMas Corporation is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.3B market cap on $646M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and -3% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $69M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.98× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 8.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
